comparison: Perfect agreement on TbMyo1's cytosolic distribution (C3, C18, C53). Both accept the biochemical fractionation data showing ~40% cytosolic and ~40% cytoskeleton-associated TbMyo1. OpenEval notes consistency with immuno-EM data; peer reviewers accept the quantification without challenge.

Perfect agreement on glycosomal localization (C9, C19, C50, C104). Both recognize this as a novel and unexpected finding. OpenEval notes validation by proteomic data and multiple imaging modalities; peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as opening new research avenues for myosin I functionality.

Agreement on TbMyo1 RNAi findings (C64, C65, C66), but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to severe morphological phenotype making interpretation difficult and acknowledges preliminary nature. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing the RNAi data as successfully addressing a previous weakness and finding the limited effect on endocytosis interesting.

Perfect agreement on CLEM technical achievement (C123, C124). Both recognize this as a methodological advance for the field. OpenEval notes it as a minor technical contribution; peer reviewers explicitly praise the exceptional rigor and successful integration of sophisticated techniques.

Agreement on specificity controls (C62, C63, C29). Both accept that preservation of Golgi, motility, and flagellar pocket structure demonstrates the endosomal disruption is specific. OpenEval emphasizes these as important controls; peer reviewers accept them as demonstrating specificity of the phenotype.

Agreement on negative localization findings (C13, C14, C54, C55). Both accept the weak correlations with biosynthetic pathway markers. OpenEval notes appropriate discussion of correlation vs. co-occurrence; peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting the specificity of TbMyo1's endosomal localization.

Agreement on TbMyo21 findings (C30, C31). Both accept the low expression and non-essential nature of TbMyo21. OpenEval also addresses C1 and C32 (TbMyo1 expression and PCF downregulation); peer reviewers focus only on TbMyo21 data as supporting the focus on TbMyo1.

Strong agreement on latrunculin A effects (C6, C7, C26, C27, C28). Both accept the time-dependent disruption of endosomal integrity and specificity of the phenotype. OpenEval emphasizes the progression and EM documentation; peer reviewers strongly support this as a central conclusion showing actomyosin's role in endosomal organization.

Agreement on in vitro motility findings (C2, C33). Both accept the velocity measurements and motor activity. OpenEval also addresses C10 and C11 (structural features); peer reviewers explicitly affirm TbMyo1 as a dynamic motor suggesting active role in trafficking, potentially higher velocities than similar myosins.

Agreement on main conclusions (C8, C69, C70, C72) but with nuance. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting convergence of evidence while acknowledging need for direct functional investigation. Peer reviewers also support the main premise but note (R16) that mechanistic details remain to be elucidated despite functional data provided.

Agreement on endosomal localization (C4, C5, C20). Both accept colocalisation with Rab5A/Rab7 but not Rab11, indicating post-endocytic trafficking. OpenEval emphasizes multiple imaging modalities; peer reviewers affirm compelling evidence for actomyosin localization to endosomal system, also noting C12, C15, C16, C17, C21.

Agreement on actomyosin localization relative to flagellar pocket (C86, C87, C88). Both accept that TbMyo1 is not constitutively present at the site of endocytosis. OpenEval notes strong correlation with actin and distance from flagellar pocket; peer reviewers accept this supports post-endocytic function, also addressing C69 and C71.

Agreement on structural features (C10, C11). Both accept sequence analysis, structural predictions, and protein purification. OpenEval emphasizes SDS-PAGE validation; peer reviewers accept structural predictions and biochemical characterization as part of comprehensive approach, also addressing C46 and C47 (FYVE domain).

Agreement on FYVE domain predictions (C46, C47). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to unpublished preliminary data requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the FYVE domain prediction and preliminary PI(3)P binding data as supporting the membrane association model.

Agreement on chromobody approach (C22, C23). Both accept successful chromobody expression and validation. OpenEval emphasizes this as first use in trypanosomatids and consistency with prior reports; peer reviewers affirm visualization of actomyosin system for the first time, also addressing C24, C25, C59 (LatA sensitivity and colocalization).

Partial overlap on endosomal localization. OpenEval R8 focuses on TbMyo1 clustering adjacent to lysosome (C21, C15, C56); peer R3 addresses broader endosomal localization including C4, C5, C12, C15, C16, C17, C20, C21. Both support the endosomal association findings.

Partial overlap on actin-TbMyo1 colocalization. OpenEval R11 emphasizes strong correlation (C25, C59, C86, C87, C88, C112); peer R5 focuses on chromobody validation and colocalization (C22, C23, C24, C25, C59). Both support the actomyosin colocalization findings.

Partial overlap on TbMyo1 expression. OpenEval R1 addresses multiple expression claims (C1, C30, C31, C32); peer R10 focuses specifically on PCF downregulation (C32, C121). Both accept the expression data and life stage differences.

Minimal overlap on biosynthetic pathway interpretation. OpenEval R20 rates speculation about biosynthetic vs. degradative pathways (C90, C91, C92) as UNCERTAIN; peer R15 accepts the model of endosomal system as central hub (C70, C72, C92) as SUPPORTED main conclusion.

Minimal overlap on life stage differences. OpenEval R21 addresses multiple expression and comparison claims (C118, C119, C120, C121); peer R10 focuses on PCF downregulation (C32, C121). Both accept the life stage expression differences.

Minimal overlap on cargo uptake and endosomal localization. OpenEval R5 focuses on cargo uptake experiments and correlation vs. co-occurrence (C16, C17, C57, C58, C96); peer R3 addresses broader endosomal localization. Both support endosomal association but emphasize different aspects.

Minimal overlap on latrunculin A validation. OpenEval R10 focuses on LatA validation of chromobody specificity (C24, C6); peer R5 addresses chromobody approach more broadly (C22, C23, C24, C25, C59). Both accept LatA sensitivity as validating the actin detection.

Minimal overlap on velocity interpretation. OpenEval R16 rates speculation about in vivo velocity and regulation (C67, C97, C68, C114) as UNCERTAIN; peer R1 accepts in vitro velocity findings (C2, C33, C68) as SUPPORTED, affirming active role in trafficking.

Minimal overlap on endocytosis mechanism. OpenEval R18 rates speculation about actomyosin not being required for endocytosis itself (C71, C116, C117) as UNCERTAIN; peer R13 accepts that actomyosin functions post-endocytosis (C86, C87, C88, C69, C71) as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on actin disruption. OpenEval R10 focuses on chromobody validation with LatA (C24, C6); peer R6 focuses on endosomal disruption phenotype with LatA (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both involve LatA but address different aspects.

Minimal overlap on post-endocytic function. OpenEval R14 addresses main conclusions about endosomal integrity (C8, C69, C70, C72); peer R13 focuses on localization away from flagellar pocket supporting post-endocytic function (C86, C87, C88, C69, C71). Both support post-endocytic role.

Minimal overlap on specificity of phenotype. OpenEval R13 focuses on preservation of other structures as controls (C29, C62, C63); peer R6 emphasizes the endosomal disruption phenotype itself (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both address LatA effects but different aspects.

Minimal overlap on endosomal integrity conclusion. OpenEval R14 addresses main conclusions (C8, C69, C70, C72); peer R6 focuses on LatA-induced disruption (C6, C7, C8, C26, C27, C28, C29). Both support role in endosomal integrity but emphasize different evidence.

Both address need for mechanistic understanding (C100, C101). OpenEval rates speculative claims about velocity and regulation as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewers acknowledge authors' caveats but note mechanistic details remain to be elucidated despite functional data, indicating ongoing uncertainty about mechanisms.

OpenEval found TbMyo1 clustering adjacent to lysosome with moderate correlation (C21, C15, C56) supported by CLEM and multiple imaging modalities. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found, though endosomal localization is addressed in peer R3.

OpenEval rates speculation about actomyosin not being required for endocytosis itself (C71, C116, C117) as UNCERTAIN, noting contradiction with prior work. Peer reviewers address related claims in R13 but do not specifically evaluate this speculation.

OpenEval rates speculation about biosynthetic vs. degradative pathway roles (C90, C91, C92) as UNCERTAIN, requiring direct validation. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these mechanistic speculations, though C92 appears in peer R15 as part of accepted model.

OpenEval found claims about TbMyo1 essentiality and life stage comparisons (C118, C119, C120, C121) supported by expression and RNAi data. Peer reviewers address C121 in R10 but do not comprehensively evaluate this set of claims about essentiality and comparisons.
